name: Zellij
summary: A Rust terminal workspace and multiplexer that separates client and server responsibilities, manages PTY-backed panes inside tabs and layouts, and routes input actions and pane updates through an explicit session runtime.

features.name: Client/server session boundary
features.description: Zellij separates terminal-client interaction from a server-side session runtime that owns workspace state and can be attached to by clients, making session lifetime distinct from one terminal frontend.
benefits: Supports reattachment to a structured workspace
Separates UI connection concerns from session ownership
costs: Client/server communication adds lifecycle and transport failure modes
Shared session state requires coordinated updates

features.name: PTY-backed pane lifecycle
features.description: The server creates and supervises PTY-backed pane processes, reads their output, and routes pane input and exit events into the session state.
benefits: Preserves interactive shell semantics inside managed panes
Makes process exit and pane state observable to the workspace
costs: PTY and process behavior remain operating-system dependent
Many panes multiply file descriptors, buffers, and scheduling work

features.name: Tab, layout, and pane topology
features.description: Zellij composes panes into tabs and layouts, with the server maintaining focus, geometry, tiled or floating placement, and workspace-level topology independently of a single client view.
benefits: Makes layout and focus state explicit and scriptable
costs: Geometry, focus, and pane lifecycle must remain consistent during mutations
Topology features increase state and rendering complexity

features.name: Input and action routing
features.description: Input events are decoded into actions and routed through session modes, pane focus, and client/server messages; actions can target panes, tabs, layouts, or workspace control rather than only sending bytes to a child process.
benefits: Unifies keyboard control and workspace operations
Allows mode-aware routing without changing pane process semantics
costs: Modes and focus alter the meaning of the same input
Control actions require clear client/session authority boundaries

mathematical_views.question: How do clients attach to servers, and how do servers contain tabs, layouts, panes, and child processes?
assumptions: Clients observe or request workspace transitions
Attachment does not prove process survival after server teardown

mathematical_views.question: How do pane PTY events transition into pane state, layout updates, and client-visible output?
assumptions: Pane and tab state are server-managed
Rendering and terminal protocol details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which client inputs become child-process bytes, pane actions, tab actions, or session commands?
assumptions: Focus and mode determine reachable targets
The model does not prove deployment security
